import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all
of whose Sylow subgroups are finite? A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that
such a group does exist if the condition of finiteness of the Sylow subgroups is weakened
to local finiteness.

Here a group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup (in
particular it is periodic), it is *residually finite* if every nontrivial element survives
in some finite quotient, and a *Sylow $p$-subgroup* of an arbitrary group is a maximal
$p$-subgroup (Mathlib's `Sylow p G`), which need not be finite when the group is infinite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ there is a normal subgroup
$N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. $g$ has nontrivial image in the finite
quotient $G/N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a finite
subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure ({x, y} : Set G))

/-- A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa [Subgroup.mem_bot] using hg⟩

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBinaryFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite (h : IsLocallyFinite G) : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun x y => h _ ((Subgroup.fg_iff _).2 ⟨{x, y}, rfl, Set.toFinite _⟩)

/-- A binary finite group is periodic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion (h : IsBinaryFinite G) : Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  have := h x x
  have hx : x ∈ Subgroup.closure ({x, x} : Set G) := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hpow⟩ := isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one.1
    (isOfFinOrder_of_finite (⟨x, hx⟩ : Subgroup.closure ({x, x} : Set G)))
  exact isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one.2 ⟨n, hn, by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hpow⟩

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all
of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

Here a Sylow $p$-subgroup ($p$ prime) is a maximal $p$-subgroup, as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`;
since every $p$-subgroup is contained in a Sylow $p$-subgroup, the last condition says that
every $p$-subgroup of $G$ is finite, for every prime $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsBinaryFinite G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that there exists an infinite finitely
generated residually finite binary finite group all of whose Sylow subgroups are locally
finite, i.e. every finitely generated subgroup of every Sylow $p$-subgroup ($p$ prime) is
finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsBinaryFinite G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsLocallyFinite P := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»

/-!

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite, finitely generated, residually finite binary finite group all of whose
Sylow subgroups are finite? Here binary finite means that every subgroup generated by two elements
is finite.

A. V. Rozhkov showed in his 1997 doctoral dissertation that such a group exists if the Sylow
subgroups are required only to be locally finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element has nonidentity image under some
homomorphism to a finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/--
Does there exist an infinite, finitely generated, residually finite group such that every subgroup
generated by two elements is finite and, for every prime $p$, every maximal $p$-subgroup is finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧
      Group.FG G ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov proved that there exists an infinite, finitely generated, residually finite group such
that every subgroup generated by two elements is finite and, for every prime $p$, every maximal
$p$-subgroup is locally finite: each of its finitely generated subgroups is finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧
      Group.FG G ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G,
        ∀ H : Subgroup P, H.FG → Finite H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»
modeling_decisions: Residual finiteness is expressed by requiring every nonidentity element to have nonidentity image under a homomorphism to some finite group.
Binary finiteness is expressed directly as finiteness of `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` for every pair of group elements.
All Sylow subgroups are quantified as `P : Sylow p G` for every prime natural number `p`; Mathlib defines these as maximal p-subgroups even for infinite groups.
A Sylow subgroup is locally finite precisely when every subgroup `H : Subgroup P` satisfying Mathlib's `H.FG` predicate has finite carrier.

The open yes/no question uses `answer(sorry) ↔` followed by one existential proposition whose group properties are conjoined; the known Rozhkov variant directly asserts its positive existence proposition.

non-trivial image in the finite quotient $G / N$. -/

  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

finite. -/

  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite (h : IsLocallyFinite G) : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun x y => h _ <| (Subgroup.fg_iff _).mpr ⟨{x, y}, rfl, Set.toFinite _⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion (h : IsBinaryFinite G) : Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro g
  have := h g g
  have hg : g ∈ Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G) := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hpos := orderOf_pos (⟨g, hg⟩ : Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G))
  rw [Subgroup.orderOf_mk] at hpos
  exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp hpos

  have := h.isTorsion (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)

The table's reading (binary finite = every 2-generated subgroup finite; Sylow = maximal p-subgroup as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`; Rozhkov's result as a solved subordinate variant with local finiteness of each Sylow subgroup) matches the statement and standard terminology, and both slots were formalized accordingly.
modeling_decisions: 'Sylow subgroup' is taken in the sense of Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, i.e. a maximal p-subgroup; this matches the standard meaning for infinite groups (and Shunkov's school), and `Sylow.nonempty` guarantees such subgroups exist, so the finiteness condition is never vacuous. Since every p-subgroup lies in a Sylow p-subgroup (`IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow`), 'all Sylow p-subgroups finite' is equivalent to 'all p-subgroups finite'.

p is restricted to primes via `p.Prime →` (rather than `[Fact p.Prime]`), following the wording 'Sylow subgroups'. For composite p Mathlib's `Sylow p G` would add nothing new (a `Sylow 4 G` is a `Sylow 2 G`, and `Sylow 0/1 G` is trivial), but the prime restriction is the faithful reading.

Binary finiteness uses `Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})` (finiteness of the subgroup as a type); x = y is allowed, so the definition implies periodicity (proved as API lemma `IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion`).

Local finiteness of a Sylow subgroup P is expressed as `IsLocallyFinite ↥P`, i.e. every finitely generated subgroup of P (as a group in its own right) is finite; this equals 'every finitely generated subgroup of G contained in P is finite'.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), consistent with other Kourovka files (1_74, 1_40); existence is stated with `∃ ... ∧` and the group is explicitly `Infinite` and `Group.FG`.

The variant is tagged `research solved` with no `formal_proof` attribute, since Rozhkov's 1997 dissertation is an informal result; a few small proven `API`/`test` lemmas sanity-check the bespoke definitions (finite groups satisfy all three; locally finite ⇒ binary finite ⇒ torsion; ℤ is not binary finite).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

A. V. Rozhkov showed in his 1997 doctoral dissertation that such a group exists
if the condition that the Sylow subgroups are finite is weakened to the
condition that they are locally finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element has nonidentity
image under a homomorphism to some finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/-- A group is binary finite if every subgroup generated by two elements is
finite. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group such that, for every prime $p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup is finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsBinaryFinite G ∧
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov proved that there exists an infinite finitely generated
residually finite binary finite group such that, for every prime $p$, every
Sylow $p$-subgroup is locally finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsBinaryFinite G ∧
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsLocallyFiniteGroup P := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»
modeling_decisions: Residual finiteness is stated by requiring every nonidentity element to have nonidentity image under a homomorphism to a finite group; this is equivalent to surviving in a finite quotient because one may replace the target by the homomorphism's finite image.
Binary finiteness is modeled as finiteness of `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` for every pair of elements.
The group-theoretic meaning of local finiteness is modeled as finiteness of every subgroup satisfying Mathlib's `Subgroup.FG`.
The Sylow conditions quantify over every natural number satisfying `p.Prime` and every `P : Sylow p G`; `Finite P` means that each Sylow subgroup itself is finite.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that such a group does exist if
the condition of finiteness of the Sylow subgroups is weakened to local finiteness.

Here a group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup, it is *residually finite* if every non-trivial element lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index (i.e. survives in some finite quotient),
and a *Sylow $p$-subgroup* of an arbitrary (possibly infinite) group is a
maximal $p$-subgroup, as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ there is a normal
subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. the image of $g$ in the
finite quotient $G/N$ is non-trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G}

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isBinaryFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A binary finite group is periodic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion (h : IsBinaryFinite G) : Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro g
  have : Finite (Subgroup.closure {g, g}) := h g g
  have hg := isOfFinOrder_of_finite
    (⟨g, Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)⟩ : Subgroup.closure {g, g})
  rwa [← orderOf_pos_iff, Subgroup.orderOf_mk, orderOf_pos_iff] at hg

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

Here "all Sylow subgroups are finite" means: for every prime $p$, every Sylow
$p$-subgroup of $G$ (i.e. every maximal $p$-subgroup, `Sylow p G`) is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsBinaryFinite G ∧
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that there exists an infinite
finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all of whose Sylow
subgroups are locally finite: for every prime $p$, every finitely generated
subgroup of every Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsBinaryFinite G ∧
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsLocallyFinite P := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»

modeling_decisions: Residual finiteness is formalized via finite-index normal subgroups (g ∉ N) rather than via homomorphisms to finite groups; the two are classically equivalent and the chosen form avoids quantifying over a universe of finite groups.

'All Sylow subgroups are finite' is formalized as: for every prime p, every `Sylow p G` (Mathlib's maximal p-subgroup, nonempty for any group by Zorn) is finite. By `IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow` this is equivalent to every p-subgroup being finite. Quantification is restricted to primes p since `Sylow p G` for non-prime p is not the intended notion.

The witness group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following existing Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74); the existence of such a group is universe-independent.
The variant is tagged `research solved` with no `formal_proof` attribute, as the source cites only Rozhkov's informal 1997 dissertation.

def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite group $G$
such that every subgroup generated by two elements of $G$ is finite and, for
every prime $p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
        (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov proved that there exists an infinite finitely generated
residually finite group $G$ such that every subgroup generated by two elements
of $G$ is finite and, for every prime $p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is
locally finite; that is, every finitely generated subgroup of it is finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
        (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G,
          ∀ H : Subgroup P, H.FG → Finite H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»
modeling_decisions: Residual finiteness is stated by requiring every nonidentity element to have nonidentity image under a homomorphism to some finite group; surjectivity is unnecessary because the image is itself a finite quotient.
“Binary finite” is represented as finiteness of `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` for every pair of elements.
Sylow conditions quantify over every prime `p` and every `P : Sylow p G`, using Mathlib's maximal p-subgroups for arbitrary groups.
Local finiteness of a Sylow subgroup `P` is expanded as: every `H : Subgroup P` satisfying `H.FG` is finite.
The main open yes/no question uses `answer(sorry) ↔` an existential conjunction; Rozhkov's known positive variant is a direct existential tagged `research solved`.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Finite-index normal subgroups and finite quotient groups are available, but there is no existing packaged predicate; the direct finite-target homomorphism characterization most closely follows the source gloss.
new_definitions.name: Kourovka.«9.77».IsResiduallyFinite
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib provides a group-theoretic residual-finiteness predicate.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite, finitely generated, residually finite group in which every
two-generated subgroup is finite and every Sylow subgroup is finite?

A. V. Rozhkov showed in his 1997 Doctor of Sciences dissertation that such a group exists
if the Sylow subgroups are required only to be locally finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element has nonidentity image under a
homomorphism to a finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all of whose
Sylow subgroups are finite? Here "binary finite" means that every subgroup generated by two
elements is finite, and a Sylow $p$-subgroup means a maximal $p$-subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov showed in his 1997 Doctor of Sciences dissertation that there exists an infinite
finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all of whose Sylow subgroups are locally
finite. Here a group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      (∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (P : Sylow p G) (H : Subgroup P), Group.FG H → Finite H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»
modeling_decisions: Formalized “binary finite” as `∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})`, so the subgroup generated by every pair is finite.
Quantified Sylow conditions as `∀ p, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, ...`, matching Mathlib's maximal p-subgroup notion for infinite groups.
Formalized a locally finite Sylow subgroup by requiring `Finite H` for every subgroup `H : Subgroup P` satisfying `Group.FG H`.
Defined residual finiteness using separating homomorphisms to finite groups. This is equivalent to survival in a finite quotient by restricting the codomain to the finite image.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has finite groups, group homomorphisms, quotients, and related torsion results, but no residual-finiteness predicate. The definition uses the standard equivalent characterization that every nonidentity element has nonidentity image in some finite group.
new_definitions.name: Kourovka.«9.77».IsResiduallyFinite
new_definitions.why_needed: The statements require residual finiteness, for which no definition was found in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
